rows.description: A teenager may not tell whether a churning stomach means hunger, nervousness or excitement, and misreads the situation. Slowing down to notice the whole pattern helps identify what the body is saying.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, confusion, excitement

rows.description: A young adult pushing through headache, tension and exhaustion for grades or work mistakes discomfort for weakness. Listening to early signals prevents the later collapse.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person pauses for a minute to notice jaw, shoulders, stomach and breathing, and asks what the body is telling them. This simple habit reveals stress, hunger or fatigue before they turn into snapping or burnout.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: tiredness, relief from stress

rows.subtype: People who feel body signals differently [Observer]
rows.description: Some people, including many neurodivergent people, feel hunger, pain or emotion in the body more faintly or more intensely than others. Respecting this, and using routines and reminders, avoids blaming them for missing cues.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Headaches and stomach aches from school worry [Actor]
rows.description: A child under pressure from exams, bullying or family tension develops real pain with no clear physical cause. The symptom is genuine, and the cause may be an emotional load that needs attention.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Tired, tense and unwell in exam season [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager during exams develops headaches, an upset stomach, muscle aches and constant tiredness. Rest, food, movement and reassurance from a trusted adult ease these signs, and a doctor should check if they persist.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager whose pain is dismissed as attention-seeking feels unheard and may hide distress or feel worse. Taking symptoms seriously, and checking them medically, opens the way to talking about stress too.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult under heavy pressure notices a racing heart, clenched jaw, tight neck and a bad stomach. Understanding stress as a body event lowers fear, while medical checks rule out other causes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A worker in long-term overload feels constant tiredness, frequent colds, aches and detachment from work they once liked. The body is asking for change in workload and rest, not only for a holiday.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Reading the body as a signal and acting [Response]
rows.description: A person who notices repeated stress symptoms sees a doctor, reduces load where possible, talks to someone and rebuilds routines of rest. Ignoring the signals tends to make them louder.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
